summary: San Bernardino County's 1926 Little Mountain lookout; replaced in 1938. The register says only concrete footers remain. Ownership and access are unclear.

facts.design: 7-by-7-foot wood cab on a 10-foot wood tower (1926); later a 20-foot steel tower with L4 cab (1938)
facts.status_note: The register says only the concrete footers remain.
facts.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection

events.note: County lookout established in 1926; 7-by-7-foot wood cab on a 10-foot wood tower
Heliograph announced in August 1927 to signal the federal lookout on Keller Peak
Residence cabin added under the tower
Keeper M.R. Jackson had lived in a tent house
New 20-foot steel tower with L4 cab replaced the original structure
State forestry department lookout station; Milton R. Jackson in charge
Brush fire, apparently started by hunters, threatened the station; crews saved it
Brush fire started by incendiary material from an army demolition squad; a cleared patch saved the station
State Forester P.S. Black at the lookout station
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register

corrections.why: The register says only the concrete footers remain. The vocabulary's 'ruins' means footings or remains only.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The county ran the station in 1926 to 1928 (the 1928 item says the county maintained the tower). The state forestry department was in charge by 1939. The register lists only the state agency.

notes_for_editor: Ownership disagrees: the register says state land, while a 1926 clipping says the county received a deed from a land company. Removal date is unknown and no source describes the site after the footings. Access is not described anywhere. Most history comes from newspaper clippings reprinted on californialookouts.weebly.com; the originals were not checked. A 1926 Calisphere photo of County Forester Tuttle at the lookout (item d8690c03daa0189041f83d4f53758d7b) appeared in search, but its page returned no text, so no photo was added.
